thread:
Ana: seeing a spike in 5xx and connection timeouts from eu-west ingestion tier, GPUs reporting repeated cache evictions and high retry counts.
Tom: any infra deploys around that timeframe?
Jean: vpc flow logs show asymmetric drops; several /24 prefixes getting RSTs and 'unreachable' from edge routers.
Sasha: starting a controlled diversion off eu-west to ams and us-west reserved capacity. using shift-ctl to bias weight away.
Sasha: command I'm running:
```
shift-ctl migrate --source eu-west --dest ams,us-west --percent 90 --hold 45s --health-checks p50,p95,5xx
```
OpsBot: migrate job queued (id: migrate-1783004567-a). applying route-tags and updating pool-weights.
Liam: pinging net-team to check peering sessions and any ACL pushes from partner ASNs.
Priya: note -- moving that much to reserves will spike billing; track cost-delta and alert finance if > 20% over baseline.
Matt: adding: ensure destination pools run sticky cache warmup so token cache miss storm doesn't tank latency.
Tom: after 90s: 5xx reduced ~55%, but p95 is +30% on ams due to burst; GPU mem pressure is high on ams worker nodes.
Jean: router shows BGP withdraws from a transit peer at 17:46Z, several routes collapsed to null0 for a short window. correlates with first errors.
Liam: net-team confirmed partner pushed an overly-broad route-map which accidentally nullrouted customer prefixes. they're rolling back now.
Priya: keep diversion until partner confirms full reinstatement and stable BGP. capture list of affected customers to notify support.
Michael: I'll map support tickets and collect error-ids from logs, linking in the incident page.
Matt: operational suggestions for runbook: prefix-granular failover rules so we don't evacuate an entire region for a handful of prefixes; auto-rollback on error-rate regression.
Sasha: agreed. adding to runbook: pre-check BGP adjacencies + per-prefix route health before reintroducing traffic.
OpsBot: migrate job (migrate-1783004567-a) finished: final weights eu-west 0.08, ams 0.58, us-west 0.34.
Ana: quick summary: transit peer misconfig -> broad nullroute -> egress drops -> eu-west GPU cache churn -> failover to reserves.
Priya: prioritized runbook updates:
- Add 'BGP adj + route-table snapshot' step to triage (capture MRT dump)
- Include an executable shift-ctl snippet with an --auto-rollback if 5xx stays > 3% for 10m
- Require cost-delta telemetry and an automated notify to finance if reserve usage > 10% for > 3h
- Pre-warm strategy: schedule async cache-populate to reach 10% warmed state on standby pools during business hours
Matt: dashboard/signal work:
- Correlate BGP withdraw events with 5xx spikes in a single pane
- Surface per-prefix drop counts and per-peer adjacency status in infra console
Tom: infra engineering tasks:
- make shift-ctl idempotent and guarded against double-applying weights
- add a 'cache-warm' job post-shift that runs a replay of hot prompt sets to populate KV caches
Michael: running cost impact calc now and will post in #finance by EOD with delta and breakdown.
Sasha: action items and owners:
- Priya: update incident runbook and open PR to infra/docs (ETA Tue EOD)
- Matt: add dashboard panels + alert rules (ETA Mon 1200)
- Tom: harden shift-ctl and add auto-rollback (ETA Wed)
- Liam/Net-team: confirm partner rollback + do peering postmortem (ETA Fri)
- Michael: cost report + support mapping (ETA Today EOD)
Priya: I'll include the concrete shift-ctl snippet and the MRT dump command in the PR. example MRT capture:
```
bgpdump -R -o /tmp/mrt-snapshot-$(date +%s).mrt
```
Sasha: plan for reintroducing traffic: 5m ramp steps with health checks and manual confirm on BGP stability.
Liam: net-team will add an automated alert on route withdrawals > 3 prefixes in a /16 and a pre-change notification hook from known partners.
Matt: cost note: while reserves were used we saw a ~26% hourly GPU spend increase; consider transient on-demand burst pools as cheaper alternative next time.
Tom: I'll add a staging test harness that simulates prefix withdraws to validate per-prefix fallback behavior without hitting prod customers.
Ana: thanks all. leave this thread open until runbook PR merges and net-team publishes their postmortem.
